observations: Top-opening chest freezer with a silver-colored lid and a central handle.
The front panel is light-colored with a large manufacturer sticker.
The sticker reads '120 HOURS COOLING RETENTION' and '3 YEARS WARRANTY'.
A power switch and two indicator lights are visible on the right side panel.
The unit is plugged into a wall socket.
The exterior shows some surface dirt and minor scuffs.

claims.evidence: The capacity is not explicitly printed on the visible side of the unit.
This refers to the internal electrical design and cannot be confirmed from a photo.
Photo 0 shows this claim on the manufacturer sticker.
The freezer is plugged in, but the cooling performance cannot be confirmed from a still photo.

claims.claim: Barely used, bought new last year. No fault at all, the motor was never opened. Receipt and warranty card available.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The unit may not be cooling or may have a faulty compressor.
risks.proof: A video showing the interior with frost or a thermometer reading.

risks.risk: The actual capacity may be significantly lower than 250 liters.
risks.proof: A photo of the technical specification plate, usually found on the back or side.

risks.risk: The compressor may be noisy or have a mechanical fault.
risks.proof: A video with sound of the freezer running.
risks.if_unproven: as having a noisy or faulty compressor

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the technical specification plate (usually on the back or side) showing the brand, model, and capacity.
Video of the freezer running with sound to check for compressor noise.
Photo of the interior to check for frost or cleanliness.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
